Spanish distinguishes malo (evil) from maligno (the Malignant One), while German böse covers both senses, mirroring the Greek ambiguity. A single Revelation passage (16:2) preserves the classical physical sense of 'painful, grievous.'"

    Enriched: The substantivized neuter to poneron: evil or wickedness as an abstract concept. Paul urges believers to 'abhor evil' (Rom 12:9) and to 'abstain from every form of evil' (1 Thess 5:22).
